calibration.example: Legible repair intake with clear labels, familiar layout, and misplaced focus after an invalid number

primary_action.input: Tab to the 6 m footbridge row, then Enter
primary_action.expected: Set 6 m and show all three closures
primary_action.observed: The value changed to 6 m; the path and footbridge read Closed, and the ferry read Stopped. The immediate capture showed the water line still moving toward 6 m.

A-1440.edge_observation: Shift+Tab to the 2 m row and Enter set 2 m. Only the path was marked Closed; ferry and footbridge remained in the list as Level not reached.
A-1440.fact_check: The initial water line matched 4 m. The immediate 6 m and 2 m captures showed transitional heights, so they do not establish the settled desktop heights. No source was provided to verify the real-world thresholds or current closures.
A-1440.strength: The cross-section gives the thresholds a concrete physical relationship, and the focused row has a clear outline.
A-1440.weakness: Rows look like status entries rather than direct-set controls; the animated water temporarily disagrees with the numeric value.
A-1440.repair: Make the threshold rows visibly actionable and synchronize or reduce the water transition so the displayed level and graphic agree promptly.

primary_action.input: Tab to the 6 m footbridge row, then Enter
primary_action.expected: Set 6 m and show all three closures
primary_action.observed: The text reported 6 m and all three closures. The immediate after capture showed the water line partway through its transition.

A-390.edge_observation: At 2 m, only the path was marked Closed; the other two rows said Level not reached. A later capture showed the water settled at the 2 m line.
A-390.fact_check: The settled 2 m graphic agrees with the text. The settled 6 m graphic was not captured. The stated thresholds and actual local conditions have no provided independent source.
A-390.strength: The diagram, control, and closure statuses fit in the mobile viewport with readable text.
A-390.weakness: The small diagram labels and undisclosed row shortcuts make the direct jump less obvious.
A-390.repair: Identify the rows as controls and keep diagram labels legible at mobile width; align the graphic and value during transitions.

primary_action.input: Tab to the selected 4 m radio, then ArrowRight
primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and list all three closures
primary_action.observed: 6 m became selected with visible focus; the list showed the path, ferry, and footbridge, and the water line aligned with 6 m.

B-1440.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m; the list contained only Riverside path closes, and the water line aligned with 2 m.
B-1440.fact_check: The displayed heights and closure list agree with the thresholds shown in the illustration. The real-world thresholds and current closure conditions are unsupported by a cited source.
B-1440.strength: The prominent discrete controls, concise list, and diagram make the requested comparison quick.
B-1440.weakness: The illustration uses abstract icons and a single sloping bank, making the physical crossing relationships less literal.
B-1440.repair: Add a brief explanation or more recognizable crossing details without obscuring the threshold lines.

primary_action.input: Tab to the selected 4 m radio, then ArrowRight
primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and list all three closures
primary_action.observed: 6 m became selected; all three closures appeared and the water line aligned with the 6 m mark.

B-390.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses selected 2 m; only the path closure remained in the list, with the water line at 2 m.
B-390.fact_check: The visible water heights and list agree with the illustrated thresholds at both tested levels. No independent source establishes that those thresholds or closures describe a real crossing.
B-390.strength: The controls, results, and diagram remain visible together at 390 CSS pixels, with a clear focus ring.
B-390.weakness: The diagram is compact and its physical meaning depends on small icons and labels.
B-390.repair: Clarify the diagram’s physical relationships while retaining the compact controls and results.

preference.reason: B makes the requested threshold selection explicit and reaches 6 m with one arrow key from the initial selection. Its water line and filtered closure list agreed at both tested levels and widths. A has a more literal cross-section, but its direct-set rows are less discoverable and its immediate captures show a temporary mismatch during animation.

decision: Round 4 is the strongest river candidate by the minimum required width. It keeps the closure result and controls visible on mobile. Round 5 tests clearer illustrations of the physical crossings. Remain experimental below 9.5.
